item.title: Artificial intelligence familiarity and use frequency are independently associated with artificial intelligence literacy among compulsory education teachers in Enshi Prefecture, China
item.description: Introduction: Artificial intelligence (AI) literacy is increasingly relevant to teachers' professional practice, yet familiarity with AI and frequency of AI use are often treated as interchangeable indicators of experience. Methods: This cross-sectional study examined their independent associations with self-reported AI literacy among 379 primary and lower-secondary teachers in Enshi Prefecture, Hubei Province, China. AI literacy was assessed using an adapted 33-item Chinese version of the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale for Teachers (AILST), whereas AI familiarity and use frequency were each measured using a five-level item. Descriptive statistics, Spearman correlations, and hierarchical multiple regression were supplemented by sensitivity analyses, exploratory dimension-level regressions, a bootstrap comparison of standardized coefficients, and confirmatory factor analysis. Results: The overall AI literacy mean was 3.48 (SD = 0.70) on a five-point scale. item.title: Reciprocal within-person associations between physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment among primary school students participating in a cooperative games-based physical education curriculum: a four-wave random-intercept cross-lagged panel study
item.description: Introduction Physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment are central to children’s motivation to be active, yet their temporal ordering and within-person interplay remain unclear. This study examined their reciprocal associations among 1,279 Chinese students in Grades 5 and 6 participating in a cooperative games-based physical education curriculum. Methods General physical activity self-efficacy and enjoyment were assessed on four occasions separated by 33, 28, and 28 days. Longitudinal measurement invariance was tested before conventional cross-lagged panel models and random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) were compared. The primary RI-CLPM used class-clustered robust maximum likelihood and full information maximum likelihood for missing data. Results Scalar invariance was supported for both measures, and temporal equality constraints were not rejected. item.title: From Affordance to Coupling: Reconstructing Foreign Language Pedagogy through an AI-Enabled Production-Oriented Approach
item.description: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is now a routine presence in foreign language classrooms, yet the gap between what the technology can do and what it actually teaches remains poorly theorised. This paper argues that the gap is structural, and that it is best analysed at the level of the pedagogic move. Taking the Production-Oriented Approach (POA) as its anchor, the paper identifies three chronic constraints in POA practice: the cost of evaluating student output, the difficulty of matching input to diagnosed gaps, and the delay between production and feedback. It then proposes the construct of an AI-enabled Production-Oriented Approach (AI-POA), which frames AI as a change in the resourcing and pacing of an existing cycle. Three affordances of generative AI (generative, dialogic, evaluative) are specified, together with four conditions under which they couple with instruction: goal alignment, temporal placement, cognitive appropriateness and teacher control. A nine-move cycle is derived, and implications for objectives, materials, assessment, teacher judgement and institutional arrangements are discussed. DIGA-FAM model (Differentiated Instruction and Game-Based Formative Assessment): Fostering mindfulness, meaningfulness, and joyfulness through interactive wordwall
item.description: 21st-century education demands a learning approach that develops not only academic achievement but also meaningfulness, awareness, and joy toward diverse student needs. However, previous research tends to separate differentiated learning, game-based learning, and formative assessment, leaving few models that simultaneously optimize cognitive and affective dimensions. This study evaluates the DIGA-FAM (Differentiated Instruction and Game-Based Formative Assessment) model to foster mindfulness, meaningfulness, and joyfulness through interactive Wordwall in poetry text learning. Using a descriptive research design, student perceptions and classroom responses were collected from a single sample of 48 students at SMK Negeri 3 Padang through a validated Likert-scale questionnaire and classroom observation, complemented by one teacher's perspective via semi-structured interview, then triangulated for comprehensive interpretation. Findings indicate that students reported generally positive responses toward the DIGA-FAM model across all three deep learning dimensions, particularly in emotional comfort, perceived relevance, and focused participation. Development of Web-Based Learning Media for Teaching Trigonometric Ratios to Grade X Students
item.description: Teaching trigonometric ratios remains challenging because students often struggle with abstract concepts, conventional instruction predominates, and digital learning resources are underused. This study developed a Google Sites learning resource for teaching trigonometric ratios to tenth-grade students at MAS TI Batang Kabung and evaluated its validity and practicality. The study followed the 4D development model (Define, Design, Develop, and Disseminate) and involved one mathematics teacher and 25 tenth-grade students in a product trial. Data were collected through observations, interviews, documentation, and validation and practicality questionnaires, then analyzed using descriptive quantitative and qualitative techniques. Expert validation scores for content and media were 91.07% and 92.11%, respectively, both classified as highly valid. Practicality scores were 93.42% from the teacher and 86.26% from the students, yielding an overall mean of 89.84%, classified as highly practical. The resource brings together instructional materials, illustrations, videos, exercises, and assessments on a single website. item.title: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF EUROPEAN AND UKRAINIAN FRAMEWORKS GOVERNING THE USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN RESEARCH AND EDUCATION
item.description: This article presents a comparative analysis of the principal policy and regulatory documents governing the use of generative artificial intelligence in research and higher education. The study examines the European Living Guidelines (third edition, May 2026), the Ukrainian recommendations on the use of artificial intelligence in research (October 2026), and the Ukrainian recommendations for higher education institutions (April 2025). It considers the circumstances that prompted these documents in the context of the emerging concept of postplagiarism, the adoption of Ukraine’s Law on Academic Integrity, and the implementation of the European Union’s Artificial Intelligence Act. Using a framework developed for this study and comprising six categories of comparative indicators, the analysis compares the documents’ legal status, target audiences, classifications of AI use and risk assessment criteria, integrity standards and disclosure mechanisms based on the GAIDeT taxonomy, restrictions on the use of AI detection tools, and models of institutional governance. Detailed practical examples illustrate how these frameworks can be implemented in research and education.
